statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. CME equity-index futures have been halted since the Friday settle and do not reopen inside this horizon, so no Nasdaq-100 price path exists in any published hour and Tail is held at a closed-venue floor. Stress stays in the elevated band on an active US-Iran tanker-for-tanker cycle whose first verified Iranian state response is rhetorical rather than kinetic, a near-10% weekly US crude gain, and hawkish September rate pricing after the August payroll surprise.
recommendation: Tail holds a 4-6% closed-venue floor across all 24 published hours, so the deterministic mapping stays EA_ON and green throughout. Stress opens at 52%, eases to 49% through the dormant overnight window and rebuilds to a 60% peak as the horizon tracks toward the 22:00 UTC Sunday reopen, remaining inside the elevated band for the whole period. The danger window is left empty because no evidence-based intraday window can be defined while quoting is suspended. Tail remains far below the block threshold; the scores would be rescored on the observed reopening path, with orderly two-way retracement decaying them quickly and repeated extension after failed pullbacks the first genuine amplifier.
headline: Nasdaq-100 unquoted at 29,544.15 through a second full day of the CME weekend halt as Iran answers the US tanker strikes with condemnation rather than force, crude holds a near-10% weekly gain and the reopening backlog builds
body: The Nasdaq-100 closed the August payroll session on Friday 4 September at 29,544.15, up 61.85 points or 0.21% from a 29,482.30 previous close, having ranged between 29,440.15 and 29,655.22. Price retraced repeatedly in both directions inside that session, which is the opposite of the persistent no-retracement structure the Tail score measures. CME equity-index futures have been halted since the Friday settle and do not reopen until 22:00 UTC on 6 September, four hours after the final slot of this forecast, so the last print remains the only anchor and no published hour can contain observable price action. The most important change since the previous assessment is that Iran's state response to Saturday's strikes has now arrived and is verbal. NBC News reports that Iran's Foreign Ministry, through state broadcaster IRIB, condemned the strikes as 'illegal and aggressive', alleged that Washington is conducting a naval blockade and economic war, and characterised the action as a violation of the UN Charter, while CNN reporting adds that Iranian officials said they would respond strongly to any attack. No kinetic Iranian retaliation and no Strait of Hormuz closure announcement has been verified. The underlying sequence is unchanged: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps fired ballistic missiles toward a US aircraft carrier and a destroyer, neither ship was hit and no US personnel were injured, and US forces then permanently disabled the tankers M/T Downy off Kharg Island and M/T Stark 1 near Jask and destroyed the unladen M/T Kylo in the Gulf of Oman under a newly authorised tanker-for-tanker policy, with CENTCOM commander Admiral Brad Cooper framing the response as imposing a higher economic cost. A rhetorical rather than kinetic answer removes one immediate rung from the escalation stack, but the doctrine itself keeps the shipping-war cycle structurally live into the reopen, which is why Stress remains elevated while Tail does not rise. Reuters reports WTI settling at 91.48 dollars and Brent at 96.28 dollars on Friday, with US crude up close to 10% on the week, Brent up 7.6% and US diesel at a record 5.85 dollars per gallon on impaired Middle East supply routes. The macro backdrop stays two-sided. August payrolls rose 162,000 against a consensus near 53,000, lifting published odds of a September rate increase, and Federal Reserve H.15 data through 3 September shows the 2-year constant maturity at 4.34% and the 10-year at 4.77% before Friday's payroll-driven move higher, with reporting placing the 2-year above 4.37% and the 10-year near 4.78% on the session. Cross-asset context from the last completed session is mixed rather than aligned: semiconductors led while software lagged, and the VIX closed at 14.53 within a 13.80 to 14.58 range, a low absolute volatility base. OPEC+ ministers are scheduled to meet on Sunday 6 September, an oil-policy checkpoint inside this horizon whose exact release time is not verified and which is therefore described as a driver rather than published as a timed event. The shared cross-asset context file was 152 minutes old at assessment time and therefore outside its freshness window, so this assessment rests entirely on independently verified primary and reputable current sources; nothing in the stale context contradicted them. US Labor Day on 7 September means the first cash session after the reopen is 8 September, so the backlog carried into cash price discovery is longer than after a normal weekend. That is published as conditional gap risk for hours beyond this horizon, not as observed structure.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours span the closing two hours of the Friday payroll session and the first twenty-two hours of the CME weekend halt. The 19:00 UTC hour on 4 September sat past the release peak at Tail 13% and Stress 52% under a mixed mode, easing to Tail 12% and Stress 48% by 20:00 UTC as the index gave back its highs and recovered. From the 21:00 UTC futures settlement onward every hour has been scored at the closed-venue floor of Tail 5% under a normal mode, with Stress at 38% through the overnight window. Stress then climbed steadily from 39% at 11:00 UTC to 51% by 17:00 UTC as the Saturday US-Iran sequence developed and the tanker strikes were verified. Every one of the 24 slots is available from published Claude assessments and every one maps to EA_ON and green.
outlookSummary: The entire 24-hour horizon falls inside the CME weekend halt, which does not end until 22:00 UTC on 6 September, four hours after the final published slot, so no observable Nasdaq-100 price path can form in any hour and the mapped policy state stays EA_ON throughout. Tail is held at a 4-6% closed-venue floor, easing through the dormant middle of the weekend and returning toward 6% only as the horizon tracks back toward the venue timeline. Stress opens at 52%, reaches a 49% low in the quietest overnight hours and rebuilds to a 60% peak into Sunday afternoon, staying inside the elevated band for the whole horizon on the unresolved tanker-for-tanker cycle, a near-10% weekly crude gain, record US diesel and hawkish September rate pricing, none of which has met a quote since Friday. Confidence declines gradually from 86% to 78% across the horizon because later slots rest on progressively older evidence with no venue available to refresh it. The Sunday OPEC+ meeting is the one scheduled checkpoint inside the window, and its effect would reach the index through crude and rates at the reopen.
